0.0.1241: After Claude Code or Codex installs, a card now stays at the top with a Start button for each one until you start your first agent.
The welcome tour has a Skip tour button on its first slide, which also says what the daily check-in sends.

Send feedback now shows exactly what will be sent before you send it, with a box for each part. Pane text and app logs are off unless you tick them. Not signed in? Copy the report or email it instead.
Websites now open in your usual browser. The preview tile (Alt+B) is for your agents' own running apps.
Panes now fix their own display. If one still looks wrong, use Fix display in the pane's menu.
Click the version in the status bar to see your plan, build and channel. Presentation mode (Settings › Account) hides your email in the sidebar and account settings for screenshots and videos.
Fixed: text could look garbled after switching workspaces.
New file tiles now get an equal share of space. Thanks to arifrhm for this contribution (#22).
When a finished worker pane stays open, its notice now names the files keeping it open.
When you send a message another agent left waiting in a pane, SoluTerminal now checks it's exactly the text you were shown and refuses if it changed.
Clearer labels in the top bar, status bar and pane headers, and Sign out now asks first.
0.0.1240: New installs now install updates by themselves when nothing is running (Settings › Devices & updates › Automatic updates: Install when idle). If yours is set to Notify me, SoluTerminal asks you once whether to turn this on, and your answer stays. Required security updates still install either way. Agents can’t change this setting through SoluTerminal’s tools; it changes only in Settings or in that question.
After you install Codex, a banner now offers Log in or Start Codex to open a Codex pane, instead of a notice that disappeared after a few seconds.
A device request whose codes didn’t match now clears after 10 minutes, so failed attempts no longer block new requests.
Fixed: the sidebar’s Files box now accepts Windows paths written with / or \.
Fixed: after switching between Windows and WSL, Settings › Privacy & security now shows that side’s settings.

Fixed: a power cut while SoluTerminal was saving could lose this computer’s pairing with your account. A WSL update that runs but doesn’t help now asks for a restart, instead of switching SoluTerminal to Windows for good.
Finished workers now also close by themselves after SoluTerminal’s background service restarts, and large uncommitted files no longer keep them open.
0.0.1239: Fixed: on Windows without WSL, Claude Code and Codex installed through npm now start from SoluTerminal.
Auto-approve now leaves a prompt for you when a very short pane can't show the menu's other options.
When a save in the editor is refused, the message now says what to do next and stays until you close it or edit the line; your text is kept.
In an embedded editor window, Settings now points you to a web browser on this computer to approve the first browser, instead of offering a button that couldn't finish.
0.0.1238: If SoluTerminal asks you to restart the desktop app after updating, please do.
If you reach SoluTerminal through your own reverse proxy, make sure it forwards the port in the Host header.
On Windows, fewer console windows now flash on screen when SoluTerminal’s background service runs its helper programs.
Fixed: auto-approve could refuse a plain Yes when Claude Code’s menu was scrolled in a short pane.

If messages wait behind text left in a pane’s input box and nobody is typing, the inbox, bell, sidebar and pane now say so, and you get an alert, including on your phone if you’ve turned on phone notifications (needs a free account). Send or clear the text in the pane to let them through.
Sidebar rows now say why a pane needs you: “needs answer” for a waiting menu, “2 asks” for open asks, both if it has both, and “needs you” for anything else.
Fixed: in the desktop app, the warnings before Restart background service, Require and Only devices I approve now wait for your answer.
Fixed: crash reports could include full paths to your own .go files. They’re now removed.
0.0.1237: Correction: earlier versions described Settings › Privacy & security › “Share usage statistics” wrongly. Sent while this computer is connected to your account, even after you sign out. Turning this on or connecting can also send earlier turns still on this computer.

Settings › Devices & updates now has Restart background service, when SoluTerminal runs in Linux (WSL or a command-line install) and can restart it safely. It reloads ~/.solu/env. Panes keep running with their old environment and reconnect. Before you confirm, it shows how many held messages and put-back receipts may be lost.

A screen at your computer that isn’t approved, while another device is, now shows “This screen isn’t approved yet” with Ask to approve this browser. In Settings › Privacy & security, Compare codes… shows a waiting device’s code large, then Codes match: approve or Codes differ: remove. It’s offered only where that screen can approve devices.
Type here now always ends with what happened. If it’s refused, the pane says why and what to do next, with Approve this screen or Try again.

The “needs you” badge and “asks waiting on you” on a pane’s title bar now open when you click them. Asks show in full, with Dismiss and Open pane. “needs you” shows the prompt lines found in the terminal.

An agent can answer another pane’s permission prompt only while Agent permissions is on and only from a pane SoluTerminal has identified as the calling program. Claude Code panes are identified through a new local bridge. If you allow it, SoluTerminal adds its own entry to ~/.claude.json; Claude sessions already running need a restart. Workers and managed agents can’t answer prompts, even with Agent permissions on.

Codex panes don’t have the new bridge yet, so they can answer other panes’ prompts only when SoluTerminal can identify their connection, which isn’t guaranteed. Claude panes are identified through the bridge.

A pane never answers its own permission prompt. An agent denying a permission request is now checked the same way as approving one. When an agent turns on auto-approve or adds to a pane’s always-allow list, it needs Agent permissions and an identified pane, and never for its own pane.
A program SoluTerminal can’t identify can no longer type into a permission prompt, or open or restart panes through the app’s web API.

A finished, idle worker with a clean checkout now closes by itself about 10 minutes after SoluTerminal sees its work merged, even if its lead hasn’t read the result. SoluTerminal also removes the worktree it can prove the worker created.

Clear on an unsent message now works on wrapped and multi-line text, on supported agent versions (for Claude Code, its native install for now). If text may remain it shows Partly cleared, and agents stay blocked until the box is empty.

SoluTerminal’s background git calls now ignore your global and system git config, except your own safe.directory (and core.excludesFile for turn diffs and git_status only). Each repository’s line-ending and file-mode settings (core.autocrlf, core.eol, filemode, symlinks, ignorecase, precomposeunicode) are still honoured for change detection.
Fixed: a prompt echoed in a Claude or Codex pane could make the pane read as needing approval, so an agent’s message was pasted without Enter and later messages were held behind it.
0.0.1236: Settings › Privacy & security › This computer can now limit approving work, answering permission prompts and changing what agents may do to browsers and apps you’ve approved. It’s for a Windows browser or the desktop app using SoluTerminal in Linux (WSL), where SoluTerminal can’t tell which program is connecting. Choose Approve this browser in the first one and Ask to approve this browser in each of the others, then approve it from one that already is, after checking the code matches.

“Require approved devices for actions that need you” has three settings: Off, Log only (accepts and counts what an unapproved browser does) and Require (refuses it). Log only is now the default when SoluTerminal runs in Linux (WSL). Only an approved browser or app can choose Require or lower it, and under Require every browser and app you use there must be approved first.

Once a computer has an approved browser or app, approving or removing devices and changing “Who can use this computer remotely” need an approved device or, outside Require, a browser SoluTerminal can identify at that computer (not a Windows browser when it runs in Linux (WSL)). A device approved without one (the first, or one approved during recovery) shows a notice on every screen until you confirm it with “That was me”. Not you? Remove it in Settings › Privacy & security.

Known issue: if SoluTerminal runs in Linux (WSL) and your only approved devices are phone apps, you can’t yet approve a new browser or the desktop app from the PC, because the phone app can’t approve devices. Until it can, add the line SOLU_HUMAN_PROOF=off to ~/.solu/env in Linux, run wsl --shutdown in Windows PowerShell (this stops everything running in WSL, including your agents), open SoluTerminal and approve the browser in Settings › Privacy & security. Then remove the line, run wsl --shutdown again and reopen SoluTerminal. While the line is there, a banner says so and any browser at the computer can approve or remove devices, so remove it straight away. Steps: soluterminal.com/help/fix-a-problem/

A worker kept open (for example with work that isn’t pushed) now shows as a quiet note on its lead’s title bar, “Worker @x kept open: …”, with Dismiss. It doesn’t count as needing you, isn’t in the bell and doesn’t notify your phone. If the work stays unpublished for 72 hours, or its lead stops running, it becomes an ask for you to decide how to keep it.

Agents no longer set flags: flags are only yours. Agents tell you they need you with an ask instead. When you update, flags agents set in earlier versions become asks, and notes about workers kept open move to their lead’s title bar.

When you stop an agent and a message is put back in its input box, agents can’t type into that pane until the message is sent, cleared or gone from the box. If you edit it, the pane offers Clear (for a single line) or Keep as my draft; agents still can’t type there until the text is gone.

Fixed: when SoluTerminal runs on Windows (not in WSL), Arc, Zen and LibreWolf are now recognised as browsers, so actions that need you, such as approving a device, work from them instead of being refused.
0.0.1235: Correction to 0.0.1234: there’s no sidebar search box. To find a pane by its handle, press Ctrl+K and type the handle without the @ (typing @ first searches the text in your panes instead). It finds panes in the workspace you have open.
The sidebar tree now has one button that collapses or expands it all. Alt+click a chevron to open or close everything below it, or press * or - on a row to open or close it and the rows beside it.

Right-click a pane or workspace in the sidebar, or press Shift+F10 or the Menu key on its row, to open its menu. A pane’s menu has the same Make lead… and Make worker choices as its title bar. A workspace’s menu has Make leads…, to make several of your panes leads at once, each with its role.
To delete a workspace, right-click it and choose Delete. Workspace rows no longer show an ×, except on touch screens.
In the sidebar, every lead now sits at the top level of its workspace, even one another lead started; hover over it to see who. A lead’s workers start folded under it.
In the sidebar, a ring on a pane’s dot means a pane below it needs you, and a folded row shows how many (for example “2●”). Leads show their role in a small label.
Sidebar rows now show the pane’s @handle, then what it’s working on: on one line in a wide sidebar, on two in a narrow one.
An agent can now make a pane you opened a lead, but only when you ask it to. You approve each one in the app, even if “Let agents in panes approve for me” is on in Settings › Agent permissions.

Agents can now move a pane to another of your workspaces, rename a workspace, or delete an empty one. Moving a pane the agent didn’t start and doesn’t lead, and every rename or delete, needs your Allow in the app, even if “Let agents in panes approve for me” is on. You can also answer from your phone.

If an agent sends a message to a Claude or Codex pane while you’re typing in it, the message now waits instead of going into your text. The pane shows who it’s from, with Send now and Discard, and it goes in by itself once your input box is empty and you’ve stopped typing.

Fixed: text in a Claude or Codex pane’s input box that you didn’t type could hold back auto-approve. Agents can also no longer leave half-typed messages in those panes, and their messages no longer carry invisible characters.
Flags you set with “Flag for attention…” are now yours: agents can no longer change or clear them.

Agents can now tell you when they’re waiting on you. The ask shows in the bell, on the pane’s title bar and in the sidebar, and your phone gets a notification if you’ve turned on phone notifications. Dismiss it with the × in the bell; it also closes by itself when the agent’s pane closes.

Fixed: if you stop an agent and a message another pane sent it is put back in its input box, the pane now shows it as an unsent message, with Send and Clear, instead of quietly holding up later messages.
0.0.1234: Messages an agent sends to a busy pane no longer get stuck in its text box. In a Claude pane, SoluTerminal tries once more if the message wasn’t taken; if it still isn’t, it waits on the pane as an unsent message you can Send or Clear. A busy shell isn’t typed into, and the agent is told the message wasn’t sent. A question an agent asks a busy pane now waits until that pane is free.
In the sidebar, every pane row now shows an × to close it when you point at it. Typing in a pane no longer makes it show as busy.

Panes an agent starts for a task are now workers. Once a Claude or Codex worker has been idle for about 5 minutes, the pane that started it has read the result, and its work is committed and pushed, it closes by itself. Panes you start never close by themselves, and nor do leads, long-lived panes with a role such as “security”. Workers sit under their nearest lead in the sidebar, and a pane’s menu now has “Make lead…” and “Make worker”.
Sidebar rows now start with the pane’s @handle, with its title dimmed after it, and the sidebar search finds panes by handle.
A pane an agent starts now opens in that agent’s own workspace, not whichever workspace you’re looking at.
Fixed: the status bar at the bottom of the window could be cut off, for example after a restart or an update with the window maximised, until you restored and maximised the window again.
0.0.1233: The sidebar’s workspace tree now keeps panes in the same order as your workspace, so they no longer jump around when something changes.
Clicking a workspace in the sidebar now shows just its top-level panes. Panes an agent starts sit under the pane that started them, and All panes shows everything.
In a narrow pane, the title bar now moves its details under the “+N” button one at a time, least important first, so the important ones stay visible longer. Its buttons now stay inside the pane.
Fixed: in a small pane, auto-approve could stop with “auto blocked” after a few prompts until you maximised the pane. It now keeps working.
Fixed: auto-approve now recognises permission prompts whose text wraps onto more than one line in a narrow pane.

When an agent sends a message to a Codex pane that’s busy, SoluTerminal now queues it for Codex’s next turn instead of interrupting the running one. If it can’t be queued, it waits on the pane as an unsent message you can Send or Clear, instead of sitting in the text box.
0.0.1232: Panes that an agent starts now appear in your open workspace straight away, next to the pane that started them, without reloading. A pane you’ve closed no longer comes back as a “Saved pane” tile.

Each workspace now keeps its panes in an even grid as you open and close them. Dragging a divider, moving a pane or choosing a preset switches that workspace to Custom; “Re-tile panes” goes back to the automatic grid.
The sidebar now shows each workspace as a tree, with the panes an agent started listed under the pane that started them.
Settings › Devices is now split into Account, Notifications & voice, Privacy & security, and Devices & updates. Voice settings sit together in one Voice group, shown only when voice is available.
The Windows background service now shows its name and version in its file details, and never asks for administrator rights.
In a narrow pane, the title bar now keeps its name and buttons readable and gathers the other details under a “+N” button.
Fixed: if you turned a pane’s auto-approve off, it could go back to its earlier setting after SoluTerminal restarted. Off now stays off.
Fixed: on PCs where PowerShell is set to block scripts, updates could fail to install in the background. They now install.
Fixed: the sidebar sections you show or hide are now saved on the computer, so they no longer reset when you open SoluTerminal at a different address.
Security: when an agent or the file viewer opens or edits a file, SoluTerminal now reads only ordinary files, not folders, devices or pipes, and stops at 512 KB.

Safer by default: agents now need your OK in the app to close or rename a pane they didn’t start, or to change its handle or working-on line. The request appears under the top bar: click Review, then Allow or Deny. Requests you don’t answer expire after 10 minutes. If “Let agents in panes approve for me” is on, they don’t ask.
When you open the desktop app, a “Starting SoluTerminal…” window now shows each step while it starts, instead of a blank screen.

If WSL can’t start because an older SoluTerminal service in another WSL distro is using its port, the desktop app now switches to Windows only within seconds and says “WSL didn’t start; using Windows only for now”. When it can find them, it names that distro and gives the command to stop that service.

After you sign in on the desktop, “Connect this PC to your account?” now waits until the welcome tour and checklist are closed. Pressing Esc or clicking outside only puts it off until the next start; only “Not now” turns it down.
On your phone, a newly connected PC now appears in your list within seconds, without reloading.

A pane’s auto-approve chip now reads “manual”, “auto?” or “AUTO”, and clicking it opens a menu instead of switching mode. Turning on “Always approve” now asks you to confirm first, from the chip, the pane menu or the command palette.

On a computer without Claude Code, a new automation now starts as “Prompt into a pane”, and “Run a Claude task” is marked “Needs Claude Code” instead of creating an automation that fails every time it runs.
If part of the window fails to load, SoluTerminal now shows “Something went wrong” with Reload and Send report, instead of a blank window. Your panes keep running.
You can now drop a file onto a terminal pane, not just an image: documents, data and code files up to 25 MB. SoluTerminal saves it and types its path into the pane. Thanks to an outside contributor.
Alerts from a command-line agent SoluTerminal doesn’t recognise now say “Agent” instead of “Claude”. Thanks to an outside contributor.
On your phone, the Enter answer key now also shows the highlighted option (for example “Yes”) when it can be read from the screen.
The pane menu now has “Resume session” for a pane whose session ended and can be resumed.
Fixed: after an update to our service, a phone, browser or Cloud-mode window could stop sending your typing until you reloaded it. Typing now keeps working after it reconnects.
Fixed: after you closed the window to the tray and opened it again, panes could appear without their title bar and their Reply and approval buttons.
Fixed: “Realign display” and “Force redraw” in a pane’s ⋯ menu, and “Rewrap” under the top bar’s refresh button, did nothing. They now work.
Fixed: in a narrow pane, the title bar’s ⋯ menu and close button could be pushed out of view.

Fixed: with Settings › Terminal & panes › “After a restart” set to “Don’t resume”, panes now stay paused after a restart instead of offering to resume. To continue one, choose “Resume session” in its ⋯ menu.

Fixed: when SoluTerminal runs in WSL, the status bar no longer says “Disk almost full” while your Windows drive still has plenty of space. It now warns when the drive has less than 20 GB and less than 5% free.
Fixed: the × on a workspace row now asks before deleting the workspace.
Fixed: in Settings › Appearance, you can now type a font size, line height or sidebar text size; the box no longer jumps to the limit while you type.
Fixed: a Focus pane draft holding only spaces, or one left from a pane you’ve closed, no longer holds back “Install when idle” updates.
Fixed: the phone pairing steps now name the phone’s real button, “+ Claim a new machine”.
Fixed: the desktop app now spells SoluTerminal with capitals in the tray, the window title and the notice shown when you close the window.

0.0.1229: When the desktop app starts, a “Starting SoluTerminal…” window now shows each step instead of a blank window.

If WSL can’t start because an older SoluTerminal service in another WSL distro is using its port, the desktop app now switches to Windows only within seconds and says “WSL didn’t start; using Windows only for now”, with the distro and the command to stop that service.
In Cloud mode, the desktop app no longer offers another computer’s installer as its own update. To update this computer’s desktop app, use “Switch to Local” in the version menu or the banner.
On your phone, the Enter answer key now also shows the highlighted option (for example “Yes”) when it can be read from the screen.

The version menu now says what an automatic restart is waiting for, and when one didn’t work. Automatic restarts are still paused for now, so you’ll see “Automatic restart is paused — use Update now”.
Alerts from a command-line agent SoluTerminal doesn’t recognise now say “Agent” instead of a wrong name. Thanks to an outside contributor.
You can now drop files onto a pane, not just images, with the same file types and 25 MB limit as pasting a file. Thanks to an outside contributor.
Fixed: a message box holding only spaces, or a draft from a pane you’ve closed, no longer holds back “Install when idle” updates.
0.0.1228: Security: SoluTerminal’s background service now refuses to start the desktop installer, or open its folder, when the request comes through your SoluTerminal account’s cloud connection (for example from your phone). Only the computer itself can start it.

Todos has been removed. If you used it, your todos are saved in a file named todos-export.md in SoluTerminal’s .solu folder, and the original files are kept. To mark something to come back to, right-click its pane and choose “Flag for attention…”.

Managed agents have been removed. The Agents section is gone and their schedules are switched off; if you had any, they were saved to a file named agents-export.md in SoluTerminal’s .solu folder, and the original files are kept. If you see Agents in the status bar, “Pause all…” is there now.
On your phone, a terminal asking you to choose now shows answer keys under it (1, 2, 3, Enter and Esc), so you can answer with one tap instead of typing.

On iPhone and iPad, the Alerts bell and the “Add to Home Screen” button now explain how to get notifications: add SoluTerminal to your Home Screen from your browser’s Share menu, open it from there, and turn on Notifications.
In the desktop app, “Update now (app + installer)” now finishes in one click: the installer runs first, and when the app restarts it completes the rest of the update by itself.

When the newest desktop installer contains an older background service than the one you already have, SoluTerminal no longer offers it. The update popover says it will update with the next desktop release.

The Inbox now shows one row per automation, with its newest report and “+N earlier” for older unread ones; counts above 50 show as “50+”. The Inbox chip in the status bar is gone: open the Inbox from its button in the top bar.
On your phone, tapping a notification from a Claude task automation now opens its report in the Inbox.
Claude task automations now see how their last report began, and keep “Needs you” for what’s new since then.

An automation that types into a pane now turns itself off when that pane is gone. It alerts you once and shows “paused: its target pane is gone” in Automations; pick another pane and turn it back on to resume.
A “Run a Claude task” automation that hits a temporary Claude error before it has used any tools now tries again once, 2 minutes later.

When a Claude task automation hits your Claude usage limit, task automations wait until the limit resets. Recurring runs are skipped until then, and a one-time task moves to just after the reset. Run now tries again straight away.

Fixed: in the desktop app, “Update installer” (and the banner’s “Update now”) now installs the team desktop installer through SoluTerminal’s background service, instead of failing and opening the download page.
Fixed: on your phone, answering a terminal menu with a single number (or y / n) no longer also presses Enter, which could answer the next question too.
Fixed: with Settings › Devices › Updates › “Automatic updates” set to “Install when idle”, an update no longer reloads the window while a message box holds text you haven’t sent.
Fixed: the “new” count on Automations now counts only automations that are turned on, so it can go back to zero.
Fixed: when the Codex engine behind a pane stops, the pane now says so (“Codex engine stopped”, with how it ended) instead of blaming its sign-in.

Fixed: with Settings › Devices › Updates › “Automatic updates” set to “Install when idle”, an update no longer reloads the window while a message box holds text you haven’t sent.
Fixed: the “new” count on Automations now counts only automations that are turned on, so it can go back to zero.
Fixed: when the Codex engine behind a pane stops, the pane now says so (“Codex engine stopped”, with how it ended) instead of blaming its sign-in.
0.0.1225: Security: the background service no longer writes its access token into its log file.

If you set SoluTerminal to accept connections from other devices and have shared its log, delete the token file (%USERPROFILE%\.solu\token on Windows, ~/.solu/token in WSL) and restart SoluTerminal to get a new one.
The app you download is now built entirely from its public source code on GitHub, by GitHub’s own build service. Nothing changes in how it works.

A new Suggest button in a pane’s “Name and handle” dialog proposes a name from that pane’s Claude Code or Codex conversation, using your own Claude Code. To have new agent panes name themselves after their first prompt, turn on Settings › Panes › Naming › “Name new agent panes with AI” (off by default).
solud version (and solud --version) now prints the background service’s version.
Fixed: on Windows, a pane whose program exits with an error now shows its real exit code instead of 0.
Fixed: a scheduled task that fails now says why, showing its last error line in the alert.
Fixed: middle-click paste now works like a normal paste, so several lines paste as one block in shells that support it.
Fixed: screen readers now say “1 file” instead of “1 files” when a turn changed a single file.
0.0.1224: Security: in the desktop app with both WSL and Windows on, a page shown in a preview can no longer act as SoluTerminal itself, completing the fix from 0.0.1223. When SoluTerminal asks you to restart it, quit it from its tray icon and open it again.
In the desktop app with both WSL and Windows on, a site you were signed in to inside a preview may ask you to sign in once more.

Panes can now have a short @handle and a “Working on” line, shown in the pane’s header. Set them by right-clicking the pane (“Handle and working on…”) or clicking the chip in its header; agents can use a pane’s @handle wherever they’d use its number.
0.0.1223: Security: a page shown in a preview or browser tile can no longer act as SoluTerminal itself. In the desktop app with both WSL and Windows on, previews get this in a later release.
With “Only devices I approve” on, voice dictation no longer sends your terminal’s on-screen text to our service.
Encrypted connections from approved browsers now notice a frozen connection and reconnect.
A quick click on the mic now shows how to dictate (hold the button, or tap Alt+S on a keyboard) instead of using up one of your voice uses.
With “Only devices I approve” on, a dev-server preview opened from another device now explains why it can’t load instead of showing an error code.
Fixed: going back to a pane after using vim (or a similar program) could type stray characters, such as 12;2$y, into the shell.
Fixed: opening or closing a tile could make the other panes go blank.
0.0.1222: New installs now start with “Only devices I approve” on, and your computer tells you when a new phone or browser asks to connect. Existing computers keep their current setting.

When a pane can’t be reopened, it now says why (its folder is gone, its conversation is open in another pane, or its history is gone) and offers a way forward: Reopen here, Go to that pane, or Close pane.

Fixed: if you switched windows just after you stopped dictating, while your words were still being turned into text, the text could be held back instead of typed in. It now goes into the pane you were dictating into.

Fixed: after you answered an agent’s question yourself, auto-approve could wait up to 2 minutes, wrongly thinking the pane had unsent text. A message you’d started typing before a menu appeared now correctly keeps auto-approve waiting.
0.0.1221: Fixed: after you answered a permission in a Claude Code pane, the pane could still look like it was waiting for you, and auto-approve could send a keypress when nothing needed approving.
Fixed: Approve with caution now checks the permission prompt currently on screen, so screen redraws are less likely to leave a safe request waiting.
Approve with caution now handles commands and secrets that wrap onto several lines, and leaves the decision to you when the full action isn’t visible on screen.
Fixed: after we updated our servers, opening your sessions from a phone or browser could stop working for several minutes; it now reconnects within about half a minute.
Fixed: after you restored a workspace or renamed a pane, the ↳ card and Started by agents could show the wrong starter, and an agent couldn’t close the panes it had started.
0.0.1220: New (beta): end-to-end encryption for browsers you’ve approved on a computer. Turn it on in that browser’s Settings › Devices › Remote devices; the relay then sees only how much data passes.

Panes an agent starts now show who started them and why: click the ↳ button in the pane’s header. A new Started by agents section in the sidebar shows what each one is doing, and Close finished workers tidies up the ones that are done.
Agents can now close only the panes they started, unless you ask them to close another one.
Messages one agent sends to another now start with who sent them, such as [from #1 Claude].
If a message gets stuck in a pane’s input box, the pane now offers Send or Clear so you can finish or discard it.
A Claude Code pane waiting at its first “Do you trust this folder?” question now shows the needs-you flag instead of looking idle.
Approving a new browser now also asks you to confirm, on that browser, that its code matches the one on your computer.
0.0.1219: Approve with caution: cancelling an automatic approval is more reliable, and switching it off and on again clears any approvals that were still pending.
Fixed: a delayed automatic approval could press Enter after you had already answered the prompt yourself.
0.0.1218: Long dictation now continues beyond two minutes and keeps your language choice. Interrupted recordings can be retried or downloaded.
Voice history keeps recovered text when you discard retained audio. Dictation shows your remaining daily allowance and stops for review as it runs out.
0.0.1217: The sidebar’s Localhost ports section is now called Services: it lists the web apps running in this workspace and opens each one in a preview at its exact address.
Fixed: a message one agent sent to another pane could get stuck in that pane’s input box.
Fixed: SoluTerminal could open to a blank window if you switched apps while it was starting.
Approve with caution: if you cancel an automatic approval during its countdown, that prompt now waits for your answer instead of being approved again.
Fixed: turning off Approve with caution during its countdown now stops the pending approval.
0.0.1216: Approve with caution: if you cancel an automatic approval during its countdown, that prompt now waits for your answer instead of being approved again.
Fixed: turning off Approve with caution during its countdown now stops the pending approval.

Move a running session from the pane menu’s “Move to workspace…” action. Choose an existing workspace in the same Windows or Linux environment. Its conversation and scrollback stay with it, and the destination opens with the moved pane focused.
If a pane moves in another window or device, a stale workspace layout now shows a warning and offers to reload. Reloading asks before replacing unsaved layout edits.
Workspace moves preserve delete protection, and a failed save leaves the pane in its original workspace.
Disconnecting a computer from your account now stops everything it sends straight away and removes it from your account, even if it’s offline.
The microphone now closes as soon as you finish dictating. To keep it ready for 2 minutes after you dictate, turn that on in Settings › Devices › Voice.
Security: your sign-in token no longer appears in web addresses the app uses.

The anonymous daily check-in now also includes two yes/no answers: whether a Claude Code or Codex pane was started, and whether two agents worked together. Turn it off in Settings › Devices › Privacy.
Safer by default: agents in your panes can no longer approve their own requests or turn on auto-approve by themselves. To allow it for a while, use Settings › Devices › Agent permissions.
New: you can let only the phones and browsers you approve open this computer’s sessions (Settings › Devices › Remote devices). It’s off unless you turn it on.
0.0.1214: Easier first run: SoluTerminal opens straight into Windows PowerShell, with no Linux (WSL) prompt before the window. You can add Linux later from the setup checklist.
The setup checklist now covers Claude Code and Codex: it can install either one for you and tells you when to sign in.
New Start Claude Code and Start Codex buttons. If an agent isn’t installed yet, SoluTerminal offers to install it instead of showing an error.
The “?” button opens a short Help menu: Getting started, Help, Keyboard shortcuts and Send feedback.
The sign-in screen matches the website, and the question about using SoluTerminal outside its own panes now explains exactly what it changes.
Voice input keeps your recording and retries if the service is busy, instead of losing it.
If the microphone is blocked, SoluTerminal now tells you where to allow it in Windows Settings.
Fixed: opening a new session on a brand-new PC could leave the window blank.
Fixed: hovering over the command palette could select the wrong command.
Fixed: the System page warned “Disk almost full” on large disks with plenty of space.
0.0.1213: Updates are now checked against SoluTerminal’s release signature before they install, so the app only installs genuine releases.
Reopening or reloading a pane no longer repeats its last lines.
Sign-in emails from the app now contain just your code.
If an update check fails, the app says ‘Couldn’t check for updates’ instead of showing technical details.
0.0.1212: Signing in is quicker: enter your email and press Continue. If your account has a password, the password box appears straight away; otherwise SoluTerminal emails you a code. New accounts are created the same way.
On a computer you have used before, sign-in remembers you and greets you with Welcome back. Not you? takes you back to the email step.
New installs follow your computer’s light or dark setting on first launch. If you have already picked a theme, it stays as it is.
In the light theme, panes no longer flash black when the app opens or reconnects.
Text that was hard to read in the light theme, such as the shortcut recorder hint and some status labels, now has proper contrast.
Output from very fast bursts, such as long builds or logs, is no longer lost from a pane’s history. This applies to panes started after the update.
0.0.1211: Agents in different panes can work together properly. Claude Code or Codex can ask the agent in another pane something and get just its answer back, without guessing how long to wait or reading raw screen output.
Agents now see the same pane numbers you do (#1, #2, …), which workspace each pane is in, what each pane is doing, and which pane is their own, so "ask Codex in pane 2" means what you mean.
Reading another agent's pane returns that agent's latest reply, taken from its own conversation log, instead of the whole screen with old sessions in it.
An agent can open a new Claude Code or Codex pane and give it a first task; SoluTerminal waits until the new agent is ready before sending it.

Codex no longer asks permission for SoluTerminal tools that only read, such as listing panes or reading a reply, and neither does Claude Code in SoluTerminal's own panes. Tools that type, open or close panes still ask.
Answering another agent's approval menu now works for Codex's menus too.
Codex panes that SoluTerminal starts get SoluTerminal's tools, connected to this SoluTerminal, even when Claude Code and Codex integration is off.
A new agent pane opened in a folder you've used before no longer shows the previous session's last reply as its own.
Turning off Claude Code and Codex integration only removes this SoluTerminal's own entries, never another copy's.
Your sidebar layout now syncs between the desktop app and your browser when you are signed in. It pauses while View as personal is on.
New, optional: get product-update emails. The box at sign-up starts unticked, and you can change it any time in Settings > Devices. Sign-in codes and security notices are sent either way.
Download desktop app links now open the SoluTerminal download page, with the checksum and install steps.
0.0.1209: Stopping new Linux and WSL workers also stops their detached child processes, so cancelled work cannot keep writing after its parent exits.
Tasks show when cancellation is waiting for confirmed shutdown and retain their working files until cleanup finishes.
Cancellation cleanup can recover after a daemon restart. Older runs without complete shutdown evidence remain visibly pending.
0.0.1208: SoluTerminal now asks before adding its tools to Claude Code and Codex on this computer. Turn it on or off any time in Settings > Devices > Claude Code and Codex, which lists exactly which files it changes.
When it is off, SoluTerminal's own panes still get its tools and session tracking; Claude Code and Codex sessions you start elsewhere are left alone.
Turning it off, or uninstalling SoluTerminal, removes everything it added to Claude Code and Codex, including its hooks, and keeps a backup of each changed file.
Pressing Esc while dictating now stops and keeps your words. Alt+C still throws the recording away.
The mic can stay ready for up to 2 minutes after you dictate, and a soft tick tells you the moment it is listening. Both are in Settings > Devices > Voice.
A silent recording no longer types a stray "Thank you." or similar phrase.
Shinoque can now use the open conversation to get names right when it tidies your dictation on your Claude plan, and it tidies short messages too.
0.0.1207: Product and tool names come out right more often: every dictation now tells the speech service to expect names like SoluTerminal, Shinoque, Claude Code, Codex and kubectl.
Add your own names and terms under Settings > Devices > Voice > Words to recognise. They are sent with your recording, never your terminal text.

Team members can switch on View as personal (account menu or Settings) to see SoluTerminal exactly as a free account does. A Personal view label shows while it is on, and your own sidebar arrangement stays untouched.
Shinoque can now tidy its dictations with your Claude plan, using cleanup written for everyday messages and notes rather than terminal commands.
0.0.1205: Short dictations keep their first word: the mic stays ready for 30 seconds after you dictate, and every recording starts with a moment of audio from just before you pressed. Turn the mic option off in Settings > Devices > Voice.
Voice history explains each dictation: what was heard, whether cleanup changed it, and when the mic was slow to start.
Dictations from the message box now appear in voice history too.
Switching windows while dictating in the message box sends what you said for transcription instead of sometimes throwing it away.
In the message box, slide left (not right) while holding to cancel a dictation.
0.0.1203: Voice cleanup can run on your own Claude plan: with Claude Code signed in on this computer, dictation is tidied by Claude Haiku on your login, your terminal text goes only to Anthropic, and it does not use your daily voice allowance. Turn it off in Settings > Devices > Voice.
Voice history shows who cleaned each dictation.
Updating the desktop app no longer hides your WSL sessions: the app stays connected to WSL while its background service finishes updating.
If WSL is unavailable when the app starts, it keeps checking and offers to reconnect when WSL is back.
When the desktop app update cannot start its installer, it says why and offers to open the installer, instead of sending you to a download page.
0.0.1201: After you sign in, SoluTerminal asks once whether to connect this PC, which turns on voice, smart approvals and phone access.
Voice shows how many dictations you have left today, ignores silence, and stops at 2 minutes.
Voice no longer sends anything into a plain shell on its own, and keeps code words like /healthz exact.
Approve with caution now works on a free account, and tells you why when it leaves a prompt to you.
New privacy switches in Settings: usage statistics (off by default) and crash reports.
Feedback tells you up front when you need to sign in, before you type.
A simpler first run: a shorter welcome that says what leaves this computer, and a setup checklist that only flags what needs doing.
A cleaner sidebar: Todos, Files and Localhost ports start hidden (bring them back in Settings > Sidebar), Schedules are now Automations and Background sessions are now Detached sessions.
The browser tile opens your dev server, or a start page listing the ones running.
One clear banner when you type on another device, with Type here to switch back.
Tidier Settings and status bar: plain words, your account and sign-out under Devices, a wider sidebar, and a chime instead of a spoken alert.
Alt+B, Alt+D, Alt+T and Alt+U reach your shell again while a terminal has focus.
